title: Forms
summary: Build a typed reactive form with FormBuilder, attach it to a template with formGroup and formControlName, validate with built-in and custom validators, show errors accessibly and read values as.
introduction: Forms are where state, validation and accessibility meet, and where ad-hoc code gets messy fastest. Angular's reactive forms keep the form model in the class, typed and testable, and bind it to the template with two directives. This lesson builds a sign-up form from scratch: controls with validators, error messages that appear at the right moment, a custom validator, a live character counter driven by a signal, and the submit flow.
learningObjectives: Create a typed form with FormBuilder.nonNullable and bind it with formGroup and formControlName
Validate fields with built-in and custom validators and show errors only after interaction
Read form values as signals and handle submission

blocks.text: Angular has **template-driven** forms, where `[(ngModel)]` bindings in the template create the model implicitly, and **reactive** forms, where you build the model in the class and the template binds to it. Template-driven forms are fine for a search box; anything with validation rules, dynamic fields or tests is easier with reactive forms, which is what this lesson uses. Angular is also developing **Signal Forms** in `@angular/forms/signals`, where the model is a signal and validation is declared in a schema; it arrived as experimental in Angular 21, so check the documentation for its status in your version before using it in production.

`FormBuilder` creates a `FormGroup` of `FormControl`s from a plain object. Each entry is `[initialValue, validators]`. The `nonNullable` builder means `reset()` returns controls to their initial values instead of `null`, which keeps the types simple: `name` is a `string`, not `string | null`.

blocks.title: src/app/signup/signup.ts

items: `Validators.required`, `minLength(3)` and `email` are built in. `noSpaces` is a custom validator: a function that returns `null` when the value is valid or an object describing the error.
`this.form.controls.username` is fully typed, so `valueChanges` emits strings and `toSignal` turns the stream into a signal for the counter.
`markAllAsTouched()` makes every error message visible when the user submits an incomplete form.
`getRawValue()` returns the values including disabled controls, with the type `{ username: string; email: string; newsletter: boolean }`.

blocks.text: `[formGroup]` connects the `<form>` to the model and `formControlName` connects each field. Errors are shown only once a field is **touched** (the user has left it), so a fresh form is not covered in red. `aria-invalid` and `aria-describedby` tell screen readers about the error, and each `<label>` is connected to its input by `for` and `id`.

blocks.title: src/app/signup/signup.html
blocks.code:
@let user = form.controls.username;

@if (user.touched && user.hasError('required')) { Username is required. } @else if (user.touched && user.hasError('minlength')) { Use at least 3 characters. } @else if (user.touched && user.hasError('spaces')) { Spaces are not allowed. } @else { {{ remaining() }} characters left }

@let email = form.controls.email; @if (email.touched && email.invalid) {

Enter a valid email address.

}

blocks.text: `novalidate` switches off the browser's own bubbles so that Angular's messages are the only ones. `(ngSubmit)` fires for a click on the submit button and for Enter in a field, and it prevents the page reload a plain `<form>` would cause. After a successful submit, `reset()` returns the controls to their initial values and clears the touched state.

blocks.title: Common mistake: forgetting ReactiveFormsModule
blocks.text: Without `ReactiveFormsModule` in the component's `imports`, the build stops with `NG8002: Can't bind to 'formGroup' since it isn't a known property of 'form'`. The same message appears for `formControlName` on an input. Every component that uses reactive form directives needs the import; `FormsModule` is the separate module for `ngModel`.

rows: String shorter or longer than allowed; the error object includes `requiredLength` and `actualLength`
Not shaped like an email address
Does not match the regular expression
Any rule you can express in TypeScript

blocks.text: `control.hasError('minlength')` checks one key; `control.errors` returns the whole object, for example `{ minlength: { requiredLength: 3, actualLength: 2 } }`. Validators that need a server, such as checking whether a username is taken, go in the third position as `AsyncValidatorFn` and set the control's status to `PENDING` while they run.

Besides `valueChanges`, every control has `statusChanges` (`VALID`, `INVALID`, `PENDING`, `DISABLED`) and the boolean properties `valid`, `dirty` (value changed) and `touched` (focus left the field). You can also change the model from code: `this.form.patchValue({ email: 'ada@example.com' })` sets some controls, `setValue` requires all of them, and `this.form.controls.email.disable()` greys a field out and excludes it from `value` but not from `getRawValue()`.

blocks.text: `FormArray` holds a variable number of controls, for example one row per phone number, and nested `group()` calls model an address inside the sign-up. The [HTML forms lesson](/tutorials/html/forms) explains the native elements and attributes that every Angular form still relies on.

questions.question: Which directive connects an `<input>` to a control inside a `[formGroup]`?
questions.explanation: `formControlName` looks up the control by name in the surrounding form group. `ngModel` belongs to template-driven forms.

questions.question: A custom validator function returns `null` when the value is valid.
questions.explanation: Validators return `null` for valid values and an object such as `{ spaces: true }` to describe a failure.
